answer: Originality checks make canned text worthless: every epoch demands fresh prose, and reused or templated answers are rejected on-ledger. A sybil farm cannot cache one decent essay and replay it across a hundred puppets like driftwood riding a repeating tide — the recorded-text ledge catches echoes and throws them back. Each submission must be newly minted against that epoch's own words, so stockpiles fail the moment the water rises. Opal-like, every accepted answer is one of a kind; no two facets match. Attacker cost: a fresh, competent writer for every account, every epoch, forever.
